newsitem.title: QATAR: Investment in GCC petrochemicals to reach $33 bln.
newsitem.headline: Investment in GCC petrochemicals to reach $33 bln.

text.p: Capital investment in Gulf Arab petrochemical projects is expected to rise to $33 billion by 2000, the Gulf Organisation for Industrial Consulting (GOIC) said.
"The overall petrochemical investment (by the year 2000) is expected to rise to $33 billion," GOIC director of Industrial Information and Coordination Abdul Wahab al-Saadoun told Reuters.
A GOIC study said at the end of 1995 some 35 petrochemical manufacturing plants in GCC states with a total investment of over $19 billion.
The Doha-based GOIC was set up and is funded by the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) which groups Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, United Arab Emirates, Oman and Bahrain.
"Petrochemical projects worth $13.6 billion which are currently under construction and, or at an advanced study stage in Kuwait, UAE, Qatar and Oman go on stream," the study said.
Saadoun said a "significant portion" of new investments would come from the private sector. by creating valued-added output.
In 1994, the industry transformed nine billion cubic metres of low value gas, which was earlier flared, into petrochemical products valued at $4.8 billion.
GCC states have developed an advanced petrochemicals industry to increase revenues which are dominated by crude exports and exploit large reserves of natural gas.
At present the region produces around seven million tonnes of basic petrochemicals like methanol, olefins and aromatics, which is projected to reach 19.5 million tonnes by 2000.
In 2000, Saudi Arabia's investment in the industry is set to rise to $23.6 billion -- 71.3 percent of total GCC investment.
Kuwait's investment would reach $3.6 billion, or 11 percent, followed by Qatar's $2.4 billion or 7.2 percent.

Saadoun said, "Given that feedstock costs account for as much as 50 percent of the total production costs, the GCC industry derives an inherent competitive advantage from lean gas which is sold to local plants for about $0.5 per million British thermal units (BTU) compared to about $2 and more in industrialised states."
The region's oil industry is still flaring around 12.8 billion cubic metres of oil-associated gas daily, he added.
